scope: Queued one-layer BF16 AFD FFN component experiment; GPU-resident inputs and one ordered device lane. Not full serving throughput or a DeepEP comparison.

hardware.placement: four FFN + four Attention on two separate four-GPU NVLink domains
hardware.network: single selected common RoCE rail per domain

method.producer: all source payloads/routing GPU-resident before timing; all variants use identical matched source graphs and live token counts
method.timed: host enqueue plus periodic/full final completion drains; startup/capture/first replay and source generation excluded
method.queue: one ordered GPU lane with one reusable pool; configured window is a CPU enqueue limit, not measured in-flight occupancy or concurrent device lanes; actual queue occupancy was not measured; zero means final-only completion drain
method.pairing: same seeded changing request trace in each repeat across variants, queue windows and modes; per-repeat throughput ratio to exact eager retained
method.aggregation: median of three paired ratios is distinct from ratio of median throughputs; observed min/max ranges are not confidence intervals
method.event_gap: interval from previous request end event to next request start event; includes host window drains and excludes within-request gaps; role statistics are medians across ranks, never sums
method.enqueue: FFN host duration includes exact-eager blocking count reads and may include CUDA runtime queue backpressure; it is not pure CPU launch cost, and the cause of longer final-only-drain submissions is not isolated
method.memory: mean FFN per-rank peak minus corresponding pre-workspace baseline; allocated/reserved subtracted separately; resident inputs baseline and native transport excluded
method.cgroup: one representative per four-rank shared pod cgroup; copies never summed
method.artifact_collection: A completed direct/window64 run had a truncated stdout collection; only its complete verified rerun is analyzed. Original partial evidence remains private, with no GPU test failure reported.
method.host_metadata: source lengths and a common selected bucket are host-known; per-expert receive counts are produced on GPU and not known to pooled allocation

limitations: Synthetic single-layer closed set of resident inputs; no model, scheduler, TTFT, online arrival process or cross-request device overlap.
Mixed source lengths and expert hot spots are seeded; only final timed output is checked, while a separate queued-burst test snapshots all outputs.
Transport and peer-wait tails can dominate throughput; queueing does not imply a consistent graph speedup.

profiling.scope: Separate Nsight Systems profiles: eight H100s, hybrid/direct, 90 resident mixed requests per variant, one repeat, matched graph sources, live GPU token counts, one ordered lane, unlimited host enqueue and final drain.
profiling.interpretation: Profiling evidence explains mechanisms. Use the separate 900-request unprofiled repeats for throughput; profiled wall times are not performance claims.
profiling.association: Host NVTX request range selects same-thread CUDA API calls. GPU kernels/copies are joined on process ID and CUDA correlation ID, even when execution occurs after the host range closes.
profiling.aggregation: Medians of per-process per-request samples (four ranks times 90 requests per role and variant). No GPU time is summed across ranks. Medians of stages do not add to the median exchange span.
profiling.gap_definition: Sum positive holes between merged GPU kernel intervals for a single request/process. Between-request metric uses all associated GPU activities, including source staging copies.

stage_key_meanings.opN: Native operation N from operation_enum; GPU time includes any waits in that operation
stage_key_meanings.gemm: Expert gate/up and down GEMM kernels

profiling.cpu_counter_scope: One representative rank per local role group; counters are shared with local peers and must not be summed. cpu.max=1600000 100000 (16 CPU quota).

outlier_evidence.interpretation: Long waits are reproduced, including request 13 and graph variants, but the underlying GIN/progress cause is not established. A blocking host count copy overlaps GPU readiness waits; its full API duration is not added CPU overhead.

conclusions: Graphs execute the same FFN kernel sequence through one graph launch; pooled eager submits kernels individually.
Graphs eliminate nearly all FFN between-kernel holes. Most exchange time remains expert GEMMs, communication, and peer or GIN completion waits.
Attention staging and graph policy are identical in every FFN variant, isolating FFN execution policy.
The direct profile reproduces long tails in GIN SendReply and incoming-request waits, including pooled eager and graph variants. Tail requests have no module loads or CUDA allocator calls.
Zero new cgroup CPU throttling is recorded during both profile runs. The remaining GIN/progress tail cause is unresolved; API timing alone cannot identify NIC versus CPU/proxy scheduling causes.
